sceneDials.label: Workflow First
sceneDials.question: What object is the user trying to inspect, change, compare, or confirm?
checks: primary object is visible before decoration
primary action has a complete state model
navigation does not compete with the work surface

sceneDials.label: Proof First
sceneDials.question: What real product, work, person, place, or media proves the claim in the first viewport?
checks: copy does not carry the entire hero
media has loading, fallback, and licensing evidence

sceneDials.label: State First
sceneDials.question: Which states change the user's decision or trust?
checks: loading, empty, partial, error, and success states are named
semantic color is not the only signal
stale or permission states remain actionable

sceneDials.label: Object First
sceneDials.question: What real object should remain legible while the interface changes around it?
checks: object identity survives route or filter changes

qualityGates.label: First-screen signal
qualityGates.passWhen: The product or primary work object is identifiable without reading a marketing essay.
qualityGates.evidence: Rendered first viewport on desktop and target mobile width.

qualityGates.label: State completeness
qualityGates.passWhen: The critical non-default state remains understandable and actionable.
qualityGates.evidence: One exercised loading, empty, error, partial, selected, or success state.

qualityGates.label: Type discipline
qualityGates.passWhen: Type scale reflects reading distance, content density, and the actual hierarchy.
qualityGates.evidence: Long labels, mixed language, and mobile line breaks checked in the rendered surface.

qualityGates.label: Dependency boundary
qualityGates.passWhen: A dependency solves a named technical gap and local code owns product styling and states.
qualityGates.evidence: Current docs/version, bundle or runtime cost, accessibility, license, and fallback recorded.

qualityGates.label: Motion purpose
qualityGates.passWhen: Motion explains state, continuity, feedback, or spatial relationship and can be removed without losing the task.
qualityGates.evidence: Review -> Apply -> Polish notes plus cleanup, reduced-motion, and static fallback checks.

qualityGates.label: Visual proof
qualityGates.passWhen: The result has rendered evidence, not only a successful build or static test.
qualityGates.evidence: Desktop/mobile screenshots or equivalent runtime inspection with console/build status.

qualityGates.label: Asset readiness
qualityGates.passWhen: Every primary visible asset is user-provided, existing/official, high-quality and attributable, or deliberately generated for the target; no placeholder or low-quality filler remains.
qualityGates.evidence: Asset source/provenance, rendered desktop/mobile sharpness and crop, loading behavior, and a visual inspection of generated or searched media.

qualityGates.label: Premium finish
qualityGates.passWhen: The surface feels authored through optical hierarchy, type discipline, material logic, precise spacing, specific content, and restrained interaction rather than decorative effects.
qualityGates.evidence: Rendered grayscale and color comparisons at desktop/mobile, real copy and assets, surface/token review, one purposeful interaction, and a recorded list of removed effects.

qualityGates.label: Reference fidelity
qualityGates.passWhen: A named or selected reference is visible through at least three translated decisions: composition, material/type, and interaction cadence; the target content and workflow remain its own.
qualityGates.evidence: Reference/build contract, side-by-side desktop and mobile renders, three named fidelity anchors, and one rejected source trait recorded.

qualityGates.label: Visual direction
qualityGates.passWhen: The build names a composition grammar, alignment axis, dominant/counterweight, type ceiling, spacing rhythm, and surface/card budget before decorative styling.
qualityGates.evidence: Visual Direction Contract plus grayscale desktop/mobile render, thumbnail silhouette check, and explicit AI-default rejection list.

qualityGates.label: Geometry language
qualityGates.passWhen: The surface has an intentional edge hierarchy: large regions use a softer or object-led contour, controls use a related smaller family, and spacing or tonal separation does more work than hard border scaffolding. Sharp geometry is localized and justified.
qualityGates.evidence: Desktop/mobile edge-map review, corner hierarchy, count of full-width dividers and hard intersections, grayscale or blurred grouping check, and one dense/non-default state.

qualityGates.label: Constraint authority
qualityGates.passWhen: Hard product and accessibility invariants are preserved while a project-owned, user-owned, reference-led, concept-led, or evidence-backed model direction can override advisory visual defaults.
qualityGates.evidence: Authority source, inherited rules, intentional overrides, reason, evidence, risk, preserved invariants, and rendered desktop/mobile/state proof.

antiPatterns.label: Card wall
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Repeated equal cards carry the whole composition without a primary object.
antiPatterns.repair: Promote the work object, group related facts, and reserve cards for discrete repeated items.

antiPatterns.label: Centered hero template
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: The first viewport defaults to a centered eyebrow, giant heading, button, and equal feature row without a product-specific reason.
antiPatterns.repair: Choose a dominant object, a counterweight, and one alignment axis; let the next proof relationship enter the viewport.

antiPatterns.label: Pill everything
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Controls, labels, statuses, navigation, and containers all use the same pill silhouette.
antiPatterns.repair: Separate buttons, rows, status tags, inputs, and frames by job; reserve pills for compact status or navigation.

antiPatterns.label: Hard-edge scaffolding
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Nested rectangles, repeated 1px rules, or hard 90-degree intersections carry the whole layout even though spacing, tone, inset, overlap, or a softer stage could group the content more clearly.
antiPatterns.repair: Remove non-semantic lines, open the page field, introduce a stage/panel/control corner hierarchy, and keep only local low-contrast dividers or exact data/safety boundaries with a named job.

antiPatterns.label: Type scale collapse
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Everything is the same size and weight, or a giant title is paired with tiny gray copy to simulate hierarchy.
antiPatterns.repair: Name title, body, label, metadata, and action roles; set a type ceiling and verify real copy at mobile width.

antiPatterns.label: Generic copy
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Abstract adjectives carry the page because the object, fact, constraint, or outcome is missing.
antiPatterns.repair: Replace adjectives with a specific object, action, measurable fact, limitation, or user outcome.

antiPatterns.label: Equal grid
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Every region has equal weight, so the user cannot tell what to inspect or do first.
antiPatterns.repair: Promote one dominant region, use a rail or open section for context, and reserve equal grids for genuine comparison.

antiPatterns.label: Default library skin
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: The imported primitive's demo styling becomes the product identity.
antiPatterns.repair: Keep behavior and semantics, then replace tokens, density, states, and composition locally.

antiPatterns.label: Decorative motion
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Animation does not clarify a state, relationship, or spatial action.
antiPatterns.repair: Tie motion to a real transition, or remove it and preserve the final state.

antiPatterns.label: Hero without proof
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: The first screen promises a product or object that is not actually shown.
antiPatterns.repair: Use real media or downgrade to a usable product surface until proof exists.

antiPatterns.label: Filler media
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: An asset is present only to occupy space, is visibly low quality, lacks provenance, or does not prove the product or experience.
antiPatterns.repair: Use the user's material, find a high-quality attributable source, generate target-specific media, or redesign the surface without the asset.

antiPatterns.label: Effect stack
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: Several decorative treatments are doing the work of hierarchy, material, or product proof.
antiPatterns.repair: Remove at least one treatment, restore object/type/surface hierarchy, and keep only the effect that explains a real product relationship.

antiPatterns.label: Luxury cliché
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: A generic luxury palette or editorial pose is being used without material, product, or copy evidence.
antiPatterns.repair: Return to the actual object, finish, use context, and specific language; let the product earn the visual register.

antiPatterns.label: Reference name only
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: A reference is named in the prompt or brief but its visible hierarchy, material/type decision, or interaction rhythm does not survive into the rendered target.
antiPatterns.repair: Write three fidelity anchors, implement the first viewport against them, and compare rendered desktop/mobile states before adding unrelated polish.

antiPatterns.label: Unbounded canvas
antiPatterns.rejectWhen: A heavy canvas has no loading, camera bounds, interaction limits, or fallback.
antiPatterns.repair: Add poster/loading/error states and a bounded static path before increasing scene complexity.

implementationChecks: Primary object and primary action are named before visual polish.
The smallest local primitive or platform capability was checked before installing a dependency.
Critical states include accessible text or structure, not color alone.
Responsive re-staging is explicit instead of relying on accidental wrapping.
Rendered evidence covers a default state and one non-default state.
Primary assets have a recorded source or generation path, survive desktop/mobile crop, and are not placeholders or low-quality filler.
A premium finish pass checks grayscale hierarchy, optical alignment, type ceiling, material layers, copy specificity, and the effects deliberately removed.
A named reference has three visible fidelity anchors in the rendered target: composition, material/type, and interaction cadence.
The Visual Direction Contract names composition, alignment axis, dominant/counterweight, type roles, spacing rhythm, and card/radius/elevation budget.
The Geometry Contract names edge character, corner hierarchy, separation strategy, line policy, and any justified sharp exception.
The first viewport is checked as a thumbnail, grayscale silhouette, and blurred hierarchy before decorative effects are accepted.
The first viewport has no more than three dominant text levels and no accidental orphan line in the target mobile width.
Copy names a concrete object, action, fact, constraint, or outcome instead of relying on interchangeable adjectives.
